---
title: "Development"
---

Set up a development environment, run the tests against a local OMERO server,
and preview the documentation.

## Setup

```bash
uv sync --dev
uv run pre-commit install
```

The pre-commit hooks run ruff (lint and format) and the
[ty](https://github.com/astral-sh/ty) type checker. Fix what they report
rather than bypassing them with `--no-verify`. CI type-checks the whole
workspace:

```bash
uv run ty check
```

ty is pinned to an exact version in the dev group, because it is still beta
and its diagnostics change between releases; bump it deliberately. It reads
`# ty: ignore[<rule>]` comments, not mypy's `# type: ignore[<code>]`.
Configuration is in `[tool.ty]` in the root `pyproject.toml`.

## Tests

Unit tests live in `tests/unit_tests`, one directory per package:

```bash
uv run pytest                                      # everything
uv run pytest tests/unit_tests/omero_screen_tests  # one package
```

End-to-end tests in `tests/e2e_tests` run against an OMERO server under
production-like conditions. Run one by name:

```bash
uv run omero-integration-test e2e_connection
uv run omero-integration-test e2e_excel
```

## Local OMERO test server

A separate OMERO server for development runs in Docker on `127.0.0.2:4064`
(user `root`, password `omero`):

```bash
./scripts/manage_test_server.sh start
./scripts/manage_test_server.sh status
./scripts/manage_test_server.sh stop
```

Import Operetta screens into it with `load_plates.sh`. Nothing is imported
without `-x`:

```bash
./scripts/load_plates.sh -d /path/to/plates -x
```

[Try it on sample data](try-it.qmd) walks through a full run on this server.

## Documentation

The docs are built with Great Docs: six sites, one per package, assembled into
one tree.

```bash
./scripts/build_docs.sh            # build everything into ./_site
./scripts/build_docs.sh --serve    # build, then serve on localhost:8000
./scripts/dev_docs.py              # root site, rebuilt and reloaded on save
./scripts/dev_docs.py --package packages/cellview
```

Use `dev_docs.py` rather than `great-docs build --watch`, which watches copies
of the sources and never sees your edits. CLI references are generated from the
Click commands, so change the command's help text rather than writing option
tables by hand.

## Commits and releases

Work goes from an issue to a branch to a pull request (`Closes #N`), and is
squash-merged once CI is green. Use conventional commits (`uv run cz commit`).
After the merge, the release workflow bumps the version, tags it and updates the
changelog. With squash merges, the **PR title** decides the release:

| PR title type | Release |
|---|---|
| `fix(<scope>): …` | patch |
| `feat(<scope>): …` | minor |
| `docs`, `ci`, `chore`, `dev` | none |

Don't run `cz bump` or create version tags by hand.
